# ONS life expectancy projections The ONS modifies their estimates of life expectancy every couple of years as part of their population projections exercise. For the last four projections the life expectancy projections have been downgraded. This chapter shows how projections have changed over time, and how they compare against observed life expectancy. This chapter works with the 2012-, 2014-, 2016- and 2018-based projection rounds, as in the original analysis. (The newer 2020-, 2022- and 2024-based rounds are introduced separately; see the note on the updated fan figure below.) ## Data The projected period life expectancies come from the ONS *Expectation of life, principal projection* datasets [@ons_expectation_of_life], published separately for each UK nation and for the UK as a whole. For each of the five populations (United Kingdom, England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland), the 2012-, 2014-, 2016- and 2018-based principal projection workbooks were downloaded from the ONS website; the raw `.xls` files are committed under `data/ons_projections/` (one subdirectory per nation, `proj_.xls`). The "Males period ex" and "Females period ex" sheets of each workbook were then read, reshaped to long format (country, sex, projection round, age, year, $e_x$), combined, and saved as `data/ons_projections/all_tidied.rds`. The download-and-tidy code is preserved in the legacy notebook (`markdown/bayes_factor_ons_e0.Rmd`); here we simply load the tidied result. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ons_projections_tidied <- read_rds(here("data", "ons_projections", "all_tidied.rds")) ons_projections_tidied ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 343,400 × 6 country sex proj_year age year ex 1 UK f 2012 0 1981 76.9 2 UK f 2012 1 1981 76.6 3 UK f 2012 2 1981 75.7 4 UK f 2012 3 1981 74.7 5 UK f 2012 4 1981 73.7 6 UK f 2012 5 1981 72.8 7 UK f 2012 6 1981 71.8 8 UK f 2012 7 1981 70.8 9 UK f 2012 8 1981 69.8 10 UK f 2012 9 1981 68.8 # ℹ 343,390 more rows ``` ::: ::: We also need observed (actual) period life expectancies at birth for the UK nations, taken from the ONS single year life tables [@ons_single_year_lifetables] and tidied earlier in this project. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dta_e0 <- read_csv(here("data", "e0_from_ons_allnations.csv")) ``` ::: ## Older projections There was a report showing how pre-2012 ONS projections compared [@ons_npp_accuracy]. Let's get the data and visualise too. The underlying data is available [here](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationprojections/adhocs/006372nationalpopulationprojectionsaccuracyreportunderlyingdatauk1966to2030), and the link to the excel file itself is [here](https://www.ons.gov.uk/file?uri=/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationprojections/adhocs/006372nationalpopulationprojectionsaccuracyreportunderlyingdatauk1966to2030/eolsforfigures12and13nppaccuracyreport.xls). A copy is committed at `data/ons_projections/historic_comparison.xls`. The data requires a bit of tidying... ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} older_projns <- bind_rows( # males read_excel(path = here("data", "ons_projections", "historic_comparison.xls"), sheet = "Data", range = "A2:BO26") %>% slice(-1) %>% select(-1) %>% rename(projection = ...2) %>% gather(-projection, key = "year", value = "e0") %>% filter(!is.na(e0)) %>% mutate(sex = "male") %>% select(sex, projection, year, e0), # females read_excel(path = here("data", "ons_projections", "historic_comparison.xls"), sheet = "Data", range = "A30:BO54") %>% slice(-1) %>% select(-1) %>% rename(projection = ...2) %>% gather(-projection, key = "year", value = "e0") %>% filter(!is.na(e0)) %>% mutate(sex = "female") %>% select(sex, projection, year, e0) ) %>% mutate(year = as.numeric(year)) %>% bind_rows( # more recent data dta_e0 %>% filter(population == "United Kingdom") %>% filter(year > 2012) %>% mutate(projection = "Actual") %>% select(sex, projection, year, e0) ) older_projns ``` ::: {.cell-output Actual 1971 69.1 7 male Actual 1972 68.8 8 male 1971 proj 1972 69.0 9 male Actual 1973 69.0 10 male 1971 proj 1973 69.1 # ℹ 1,580 more rows ``` ::: ::: Visualise. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} older_projns %>% filter(projection != "Actual") %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = e0, group = projection, colour = projection)) + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~sex) + geom_line(aes(x = year, y = e0), size = as.character(projection) %>% paste(., "proj")) %>% filter(projection != "2012 proj") ) %>% filter(year <= 2040) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = e0, group = projection, colour = projection)) + geom_line() ($e_0$ at birth) change over time between countries? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ons_projections_tidied %>% filter(age == 0) %>% filter(year >= 2010) %>% mutate(proj_year = factor(proj_year)) %>% mutate(sex = case_when( sex == 'm' ~ 'male', sex == 'f' ~ 'female', TRUE ~ NA_character_ )) %>% mutate(country = factor(country, levels = c("UK", "England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland"))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = ex, group = proj_year, colour = proj_year)) + facet_grid(country ~ sex) + geom_line() + labs( x = "Year", y = "Life expectancy at birth (years)", title = "ONS projections for life expectancy at birth", colour = "ONS Projection\nYear" ) ggsave(here("figures", "ons_life_expectancy_projections.png"), height = 25, width = 25, units = "cm", dpi = 300) ggsave(here("bayes_paper", "figures", "A06_recentONSprojns_uknations.png"), height = 25, width = 25, units = "cm", dpi = 300) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](03_ons_projections_files/figure-html/fig-recent-projns-uk-nations-1.png){#fig-recent-projns-uk-nations width=960} ::: ::: ### Change in projections - annual increases For each of these projections, what's the implied expected improvement level? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ons_projections_tidied %>% filter(age == 0) %>% filter(year >= 2019) %>% mutate(sex = case_when( sex == 'm' ~ 'male', sex == 'f' ~ 'female', TRUE ~ NA_character_ )) %>% group_by(sex, country, proj_year) %>% arrange(year) %>% mutate(ch_e0 = ex - lag(ex)) %>% filter(!is.na(ch_e0)) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(country = factor(country, levels = c("UK", "England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland"))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = ch_e0, group = factor(proj_year), colour = factor(proj_year), shape = factor(proj_year))) + geom_point() + geom_line() + facet_grid(country ~ sex) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + labs( x = "Year", y = "Change in Life expectancy at birth (years)", title = "ONS projections for annual life expectancy change at birth", colour = "ONS Projection\nYear", shape = "ONS Projection\nYear" ) ggsave(here("figures", "ons_life_expectancy_projections_change.png"), height = 25, width = 25, units = "cm", dpi = 300) ggsave(here("bayes_paper", "figures", "A07_recentch_e0_ONSprojns_uknations.png"), height = 25, width = 25, units = "cm", dpi = 300) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](03_ons_projections_files/figure-html/fig-projns-annual-increases-1.png){#fig-projns-annual-increases width=960} ::: ::: So, the projections involve adding varying numbers of increments of 0.1 life expectancy gain per year. Values within these intervals are created by changing the numbers of years of 0.2, 0.1 and 0.0 gain. ### Projections at all ages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ex_projns_male <- ons_projections_tidied %>% filter(sex == "m") %>% mutate(country = factor(country, levels = c("UK", "England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland"))) %>% mutate(proj_year = factor(proj_year)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = age, fill = ex)) + geom_tile() + scale_fill_viridis_c() + coord_fixed() + facet_grid(country ~ proj_year) + labs( x = "Year", y = "Age in years", title = "Males" ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ex_projns_female <- ons_projections_tidied %>% filter(sex == "f") %>% mutate(country = factor(country, levels = c("UK", "England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland"))) %>% mutate(proj_year = factor(proj_year)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = age, fill = ex)) + geom_tile() + scale_fill_viridis_c() + coord_fixed() + facet_grid(country ~ proj_year) + labs( x = "Year", y = "Age in years", title = "Females" ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # The original notebook combined the two panels with ggpubr::ggarrange(); ggpubr is # not available in this environment, so patchwork is used to produce the same # side-by-side arrangement. ex_projns_male + ex_projns_female ggsave(here("bayes_paper", "figures", "A08_ons_ex_heatmap.png"), width = 35, height = 27, units = "cm", dpi = 300) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](03_ons_projections_files/figure-html/fig-ex-heatmap-1.png){#fig-ex-heatmap width=1296} ::: ::: ### Change in projections at all ages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ch_proj_male <- ons_projections_tidied %>% group_by(country, sex, age, year) %>% arrange(proj_year) %>% mutate(ch_ex_proj = ex - lag(ex)) %>% filter(!is.na(ch_ex_proj)) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(country = factor(country, levels = c("UK", "England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland"))) %>% filter(year >= 2020) %>% filter(sex == "m") %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, age, fill = ch_ex_proj)) + geom_tile() + coord_fixed() + facet_grid(country ~ proj_year) + scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", limits = c(-1.5, 1.5)) + labs( x = "Year", y = "Age in years", fill = "Change in ex", title = "Males, change from last projection" ) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) ch_proj_female <- ons_projections_tidied %>% group_by(country, sex, age, year) %>% arrange(proj_year) %>% mutate(ch_ex_proj = ex - lag(ex)) %>% filter(!is.na(ch_ex_proj)) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(country = factor(country, levels = c("UK", "England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland"))) %>% filter(year >= 2020) %>% filter(sex == "f") %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, age, fill = ch_ex_proj)) + geom_tile() + coord_fixed() + facet_grid(country ~ proj_year) + scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", limits = c(-1.5, 1.5)) + labs( x = "Year", y = "Age in years", fill = "Change in ex", title = "Females, change from last projection" ) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) ``` ::: And as a 2x1 table. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ggpubr::ggarrange() replaced with the equivalent patchwork arrangement (see above). ch_proj_male + ch_proj_female ggsave(here("bayes_paper", "figures", "A09_ons_ch_ex_heatmap.png"), width = 25, height = 27, units = "cm", dpi = 300) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](03_ons_projections_files/figure-html/fig-ch-ex-heatmap-1.png){#fig-ch-ex-heatmap width=960} ::: ::: ## Summaries ### Average projected improvement Let's summarise this: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ons_projections_summarised <- ons_projections_tidied %>% filter(age == 0) %>% filter(year >= 2019) %>% group_by(sex, country, proj_year) %>% arrange(year) %>% mutate(ch_e0 = ex - lag(ex)) %>% summarise( mean_ch_e0 = mean(ch_e0, na.rm = TRUE), sd_ch_e0 = sd(ch_e0, na.rm = TRUE) ) ons_projections_summarised ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 40 × 5 # Groups: sex, country [10] sex country proj_year mean_ch_e0 sd_ch_e0 1 f England 2012 0.135 0.0482 2 f England 2014 0.127 0.0447 3 f England 2016 0.113 0.0337 4 f England 2018 0.0918 0.0344 5 f Northern Ireland 2012 0.137 0.0536 6 f Northern Ireland 2014 0.129 0.0458 7 f Northern Ireland 2016 0.117 0.0380 8 f Northern Ireland 2018 0.0959 0.0351 9 f Scotland 2012 0.140 0.0495 10 f Scotland 2014 0.131 0.0468 # ℹ 30 more rows ``` ::: ::: As a wide table, mean (SD) of projected annual $e_0$ gain by nation, sex and projection round. (The original notebook also wrote this table to a styled Excel workbook, `bayes_paper/tables/M03_ons_proj_improvements_sd.xlsx`; that formatting code has been dropped here.) ::: {#tbl-proj-improvements .cell} ```{.r .cell-code} table_wide <- ons_projections_summarised %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(Sex = case_when( sex == 'f' ~ 'Female', sex == 'm' ~ 'Male', TRUE ~ NA_character_ )) %>% rename(Country = country) %>% mutate(Country = ifelse(Country == "UK", "United Kingdom", Country)) %>% mutate(Country = factor(Country, levels = c("United Kingdom", "England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland"))) %>% unite(Sex, proj_year, col = "sex_proj") %>% select(Country, sex_proj, mean_ch_e0, sd_ch_e0) %>% mutate(text = glue::glue("{format(mean_ch_e0, digits=2)} ({format(sd_ch_e0, digits=2)})")) %>% select(Country, sex_proj, text) %>% spread(sex_proj, text) %>% set_names(c("Country", rep(c("2012", "2014", "2016", "2018"), 2))) table_wide %>% kable() %>% kable_styling() %>% add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Female" = 4, "Male" = 4)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

Assumed rates of improvement are around 17.5% higher than observed in the 2010s for females, and around 13% higher than observed in the 2010s for males. To put more simply: the 2012 ONS projection assumed the rate of improvement would be the midpoint between the 1990 and 2010-11 rates, and subsequent projections have tended increasingly towards the post-2010 improvement levels. They have largely been responsive to the new and much slowed life expectancy gains. The before period used in the Bayes Factor calculations is 1991 onwards. Let's identify what the average improvement was over this period. ::: {#tbl-uk-gain-1991-2010 .cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dta_e0 %>% filter(population == "United Kingdom") %>% filter(between(year, 1990, 2010)) %>% group_by(sex) %>% arrange(year) %>% mutate(ch_e0 = e0 - lag(e0)) %>% filter(!is.na(ch_e0)) %>% summarise(mean_ch_e0 = mean(ch_e0), var_ch_e0 = var(ch_e0)) %>% kable(digits = 3) %>% kable_styling() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
